name: fchownat
synopsis: int fchownat(int dirfd, const char *pathname, uid_t owner, gid_t group, int flags);
description: The fchownat() system call changes the owner and group of a file, similar to chown(), but allows the file to be specified relative to a directory file descriptor and includes flags to control behavior such as not following symbolic links.

parameters.name: dirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor, or AT_FDCWD to use the current working directory.

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: Path to the file; if relative, it is resolved relative to dirfd.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: The new owner user ID; specify -1 to leave unchanged.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: The new group ID; specify -1 to leave unchanged.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Bit mask of flags, such as AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW or AT_EMPTY_PATH, to modify behavior.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Search permission is denied on a component of the path prefix.
pathname is relative but dirfd is neither AT_FDCWD nor a valid file descriptor.
pathname points outside your accessible address space.
A low-level I/O error occurred while modifying the inode.
Too many symbolic links were encountered in resolving pathname.
A component of the path prefix is not a directory, or pathname is relative and dirfd is not a directory.
The calling process did not have the required permissions to change owner and/or group, or the file is marked immutable.
The named file resides on a read-only filesystem.

bugs: Behavior when root changes ownership of an executable file may vary depending on kernel version, and POSIX does not specify this clearly.
versions: Available since glibc 2.10 and Linux 2.6.39 for certain flags.
